front: Finish Grandpa's saying: "Treat every firearm as if it is ..."
back: Loaded. Every gun, every time. Tradition: rule 1 of ACTS, Assume every firearm is loaded (85%).
Never point a gun at anything you do not want to shoot. Tradition: Control the muzzle (85%).

front: What must you know besides your target?
back: What is beyond it. Look past the animal; the sky is never a backstop. Tradition (85%).

front: Where does your trigger finger live until you decide to shoot?
back: Straight along the stock, outside the trigger guard. Tradition: the T in ACTS (85%).
"... you are not shooting." Never shoot at a sound or a movement (85%, Texas hunter education). Opinion, widely taught.

front: New York 1989 to 1995: share of 'mistaken for game' victims not wearing orange?
back: 94% (117 of 125) (90%, US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention). Tradition: wear orange so the next hunter sees a person.

front: Fence, log, creek, truck, boat: what first?
back: Unload. Lay it across with the muzzle away, cross, check the barrel. Tradition (85%).
... alcohol do not mix. No alcohol or drugs before or while handling a gun. Tradition (85%).
Trip planning, training, taking the essentials (85%). Tell someone where you go and when you are back.
About 1 minute of cold shock, about 10 minutes of useful movement, up to about 1 hour before you pass out (85%). Wear the PFD zipped.
"... hunt somewhere else." Keep the wind from the animal to you. Tradition; scent and movement beat colour (85%).
"... new wind." Terrain bends wind; check it again (80%). Opinion.
Sinks; climbs. Calm mornings slide downhill until the sun warms the slope (75 to 80%). Tradition.

front: Wind check shows a swirl. Grandpa says?
back: "A swirl is a no. Back out, come back." Opinion (Tip).

front: Red sky at night, red sky at morning?
back: Night: dry air coming from the west. Morning: weather may follow. Partly true where weather moves west to east (75%, Met Office).
Rain or snow soon, sometimes. Ice crystal cloud often runs ahead of a warm front, but not always (65%).

front: Do deer feed hard before a storm front?
back: Studies disagree. Penn State found no meaningful effect of oncoming winter storms (75%). Opinion; go when you can.

front: Penn State GPS: deer on windy days and nights?
back: More movement on windy days, less on windy nights (80%). The 'deer lie up in a gale' saying is mixed.

front: Which weather factor most influenced deer movement in a Mississippi State study?
back: Temperature (65%, secondary). 'Cold snaps move deer' has some support; a Texas study disagreed.
"... the day you can go." Dawn and dusk beat moon and weather in collar studies (85%). Opinion.
"... find the animal." Forage best described mule deer feeding sites (85%). Tradition.

front: Penn State: share of hunters within 0.5 km of a road?
back: 73% (85%). Average farthest point 0.84 km; hunters said 2.23 km. Walk past where the others stop.
"... walk less." Let the spotting scope do the walking (80%, Mule Deer Foundation). Tradition.

front: What gives a deer away in timber?
back: A flat back line among upright trunks, an ear or tail flick, a patch of white (70%). Look for a piece, not the whole animal.
"... the middle." Where cover meets food (75%). Tradition. On grassland, hunt the folds.
Large forest patches with hiding cover, away from open roads (80%). Go where the pressure is not.
"... scouting report in the valley." 88% of surveyed Idaho landowners say yes when asked first (80%).
"... the light." Bucks often bed early; set up before first light (80%, Mule Deer Foundation).

front: Cold morning, hot noon: where do deer bed?
back: Cold: first sun. Hot: shade. Temperature and canopy drove mule deer bed choice (85%). Opinion.
"... small spots." Remote brushy draws protected Montana elk (70%). Opinion.
Stand at least 10 times longer than you walk (85%, hunter education). Tradition.

front: "If you think you are going slow enough, ..."
back: "... halve it." 3 to 5 m then stop; or one step every 30 seconds (65 to 75%). Tradition.
Head down, you move. Head up, you are a stump. Movement gives you away (85%). Opinion.
Never walk the top. Come up below the crest and peek. A human outline spooks game (85%). Tradition.
"... you are a stump." Freeze until it looks away. Opinion (Tip).
"... do the walking." Sit on a trail, pinch or edge. 72% of Penn State hunters sat still in the morning (85%). Opinion.

front: How long did collared bucks avoid a stand after one sit, in one study?
back: About 3 days (60%, secondary). The best stand is the one the deer do not know you use.
"... glass it one more time." Look longer, look smarter (80%, Mule Deer Foundation). Tradition.
"... you know where the deer is." Agree zones of fire (85%). Tradition.

front: Still hunting: where do your eyes go at each stop?
back: Into the woods ahead and to the sides, not at your feet (85%, hunter education). Tradition.

front: "You can fool the eyes, you can fool the ears, ..."
back: "... you will never fool the nose." Play the wind. Tradition.
"... then decide." A 4 point buck has 4 tines on one antler, not counting the brow tine (99%, synopsis page 4).

front: Can you age a buck by points?
back: No: points are not a reliable age guide (90%, BC account). Read the body before the bone. Opinion.
"... the does. The buck will find them before you find him." Tradition.

front: A white tail flags and bounds away. Grandpa?
back: "A flag in the air means goodbye. Let it go." Running shots are poor shots. Tradition.

front: Spooked mule deer behaviour Grandpa counts on?
back: It often stops to look back (60%). Old bucks often do not. Tradition.

front: Daylight buck visits to stand areas, weeks 1 to 3 versus week 13 (one study)?
back: About 1 in 3, then about 1 in 20 (60%, secondary). Hunt the trail, not the field.
"... eat the shoulders." Heart and lung area is the vital zone (85%). Tradition.

front: Bedded mule deer: eyes and nose?
back: Watches below, smells behind (opinion). Science measured temperature and canopy, not wind (85%).

front: Which colour stands out to deer: orange or blue?
back: Blue. Deer cannot tell orange from green (85%, National Deer Association). Wear orange, skip blue.

front: Cow moose and calf: Grandpa's rule?
back: Never get between them. In Alaska moose injure more people than bears each year (65%). Tradition.

front: Bull moose knee deep in the lake. Shoot?
back: Wait for dry ground. A moose is too heavy to drag out of water (60%). Opinion.
"... before the shot." Moose carcasses run hundreds of kilograms (90%). Tradition.
Wait longer than you think. Bulls can come slow and silent (50%, Tip). Opinion.
"... you want to hunt tomorrow." Some Montana elk moved over 10 km in the first days (65%). Opinion.
"... than you want to." Set up right first; volume does not matter (65%). Opinion.
Bedded in dark timber near the food (Tip). Elk chose big forest patches with hiding cover (80%). Tradition.

front: Why watch a lone bear five minutes?
back: Spring cubs lag behind their mother (85%). In BC a cub, yearling, or bear with them is off limits (99%).

front: Big ears, long legs on a black bear means?
back: Young bear or sow. Big boars look small eared with thick legs (60 to 70%). Opinion.
71 °C (160 °F) inside. Freezing does not kill the northern Trichinella (90%).

front: Ducks land into the wind. So the wind goes where?
back: At your back, so they land facing you (85%, Ducks Unlimited). Tradition.

front: Landing hole distance, Ducks Unlimited sweet spot?
back: About 18 m (20 yd) in front of the blind (80%). Put decoys where you do not want them to land.

front: Call to the tail or the face?
back: The tail. Quiet when birds come at you (70%). Tradition.

front: "If you can see the duck's eye, ..."
back: "... it can see yours." A bare face or hands flare ducks (70%). Opinion.

front: When do you stand up on decoying ducks?
back: When they commit: wings cupped, feet down. Early shots are long shots (65 to 75%). Tradition.

front: Ducks Unlimited: many self taught hunters struggle past what range on crossers?
back: About 27 m (30 yd) (85%). If you have to wonder if it is in range, it is not.

front: Covey rise: how many birds do you shoot at?
back: One, then the next. Pick a single bird (85%, Kentucky wildlife agency). Tradition.
"... before you shoot the next." Mark the fall and go straight to it. Opinion.

front: Where do you never hunt waterfowl, by tradition?
back: The roost. Hunting near it can push birds off (65%). Hunt where they feed or fly.
"... not the goose." Set up where they fed the evening before (65%). Tradition.
"... miss small." One hair, not the whole deer. Origin unsettled (Tip). Tradition.

front: "If you can get lower, get lower. If you can get closer, ..."
back: "... get closer." Close shots forgive errors (75%). Tradition.
Yours, not the rifle's. Beyond your competent range you risk crippling (85%, Ducks Unlimited). Opinion.
Broadside or quartering away, still, near leg forward (85%, hunter education). Tradition.
"... then wait it." Use landmarks for where it stood and vanished (85%, National Deer Association).

front: National Deer Association waits: liver, guts?
back: Liver 8 to 10 hours, guts 10 to 12 hours; heart or lungs a few minutes with a rifle (85%). Pushed early, lost forever.

front: Deer drops like a stone. Grandpa?
back: Down is not dead. Spine shock can wear off in about a minute (85%). Reload, watch, approach from the back.

front: No blood at the hit site means a miss?
back: No. Check for hair and bone and search (75%). Read the hit site slowly.

front: Where do you walk on a blood trail?
back: Beside it, flagging each spot. You may need it twice (85%). Opinion.

front: Leg or bone hit: wait or go?
back: Go now, ready for a follow up shot (85%, National Deer Association). Finish the one you started.

front: Penn State Extension target carcass temperature?
back: 3 to 4 °C (35 to 40 °F), quickly (90%). Cold meat, clean meat, good meat.
The hide holds heat; removing it lets meat cool faster (90%, Ohio). A hide is a winter coat.
No. Plastic traps heat and moisture; use cloth game bags (65%). Tradition.

front: How long to hang venison at home?
back: 2 to 3 days at 4 °C or below, at most (90%, Penn State Extension). Aging is not necessary for sausage.
Wet cotton loses insulation and dries slowly (70%). True in cold and wet; overstated on warm days.
"... start cold." Start with fewer layers so you do not sweat; add layers when you stop (70%). Tradition.
"... and one is none." Back up what your life depends on: fire, light, navigation. Military saying (70%).

front: Sharp knife or dull knife: which is safer?
back: Sharp. Dull knives slip and need more force (80%, university extension). Tradition.

front: Bear country camp: food and meat how far from your bed?
back: At least 100 m (80%, Alberta BearSmart). A clean camp is a quiet camp.

front: When do you check your rifle's zero?
back: Before the season, after a bump, after air travel (65%). Shoot it before you hunt it.
Ethical, sportsmanlike, lawful (85%, Boone and Crockett Club). Give the animal a fair chance to escape.
"... the one you never have to explain." Tradition.
Leave it open. Leave every gate as you found it unless the owner says otherwise (80%).
Never assume it still stands. Ask again, in writing (80%, Idaho Fish and Game).
"... than you found it." Baden Powell, 1941 (80%). Pack it in, pack it out.
"... you eat it." Hunters are legally and ethically bound to take the edible meat (85%).
"... knife second." Cancel the licence before you touch the knife. Rules: Rule Book.
Do not confront. Note details, call RAPP 1 877 952 7277 (95%).
"... Take somebody." Mentor a new hunter when you are ready. BC Wildlife Federation runs Learn to Hunt (80%).

front: Where does BC's licence conservation surcharge go?
back: The Habitat Conservation Trust Foundation, since 1981 (80%). Hunters paid for the wild.
